newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - February 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - February 24.

text.p: The following were the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

First civilian passenger bus travels on newly cleared northern Medawachchiya-Mannar road for the first time in 10 years on Saturday, defence sources say. The road was recently cleared as part of operation 'Edi bala' launched on February 4.
President Chandrika Kumaratunga asks people at an election rally to elect candidates with no criminal record at the March 21 local government polls.

Opposition and United National Party (UNP) leader Ranil Wickremesinghe says those unwilling to abide by course of action taken over recent the recent killing of a ruling coalition MP can leave the party. A UNP MP and a former UNP mayor of the area in central Sri Lanka are in custody in connection with the killing two weeks ago of Nalanda Ellawala at Kuruwita.

Police continue to transfer officers out of Ratnapura where ruling party lawmaker Nalanda Ellawala was gunned down recently. There were public protests following the assassination and police stations in the area were attacked by angry mobs.
High level investigation is launched into the recent crashes involving Air Force aircraft, defence sources say.
Two men remanded in connection with death of school boy at private zoo in southern Sri Lanka. The boy was attacked by a lion while posing for pictures with the animal.
Special intelligence team investigates Saturday's crash of Air Force plane soon after take-off from Ratmalana, a Colombo suburb.
President Kumaratunga tells public to elect candidates with clean track record at forthcoming mini-poll.
